# I Tried 5 AI Side Hustles in 2026 — Here’s What Actually Made Money

[![Grifrag](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fill:32:32/0*RF5r3j9cmdLVpwbo.jpg)](https://medium.com/@grifrag?source=post_page---byline--32dc1c52b9b9-----------------------------------------)

Share

Everyone is talking about making money with AI. But most articles give you a list of ideas with zero proof they actually work. I decided to test five of the most hyped AI side hustles myself over the past few months — and the results surprised me.

Some flopped completely. One made me more money than my part-time job. Here is an honest breakdown.

1. AI-Generated Content for Blogs (Verdict: Disappointing)

This was the obvious first choice. Dozens of YouTube channels promised you could make thousands a month writing AI blog content for small businesses. The reality is different. Yes, you can produce content fast. But small business owners in 2026 are not paying much for generic AI articles — they can generate them too. I pitched 30 businesses and closed 2. Both paid under $50 per article and stopped after three pieces when they realized traffic was not moving. The market for pure AI content writing has become extremely competitive and the prices have collapsed. Unless you have a niche angle or strong SEO expertise to offer alongside the writing, this one is a grind for very little return.

2\. AI Automation for Small Businesses (Verdict: Solid Income)

This one surprised me. Small businesses — restaurants, salons, clinics, law firms — are drowning in repetitive tasks. Answering the same customer questions, following up on appointments, sending invoices, routing emails. Tools like Make, Zapier, and now a dozen AI-native platforms make it possible to automate most of this without writing a single line of code. I started offering simple automation packages: a chatbot that answers FAQs, an appointment reminder sequence, an automatic review request after service. I charged between $300 and $800 per setup depending on complexity, plus a small monthly retainer for maintenance. Within two months I had five clients. The key insight is that you are not selling technology — you are selling time back to a business owner who is exhausted. Frame it that way and the sales conversation becomes much easier.

3\. AI Video Faceless Channels (Verdict: Slow Burn)

AI video tools like Runway, Sora, and InVideo have made it possible to produce YouTube-style explainer videos without ever showing your face or recording your voice. The content looks professional. The problem is distribution. YouTube is saturated with faceless AI channels all competing for the same eyeballs, and the algorithm is getting better at identifying low-effort AI content. I posted 20 videos across three months and earned about $40 from ad revenue. Not nothing, but not a business. Where this model does work is if you pair it with a newsletter or digital product. The video becomes a traffic source, not the revenue source itself. Treat it as top-of-funnel marketing for something else and the economics start to make sense.

4\. Selling AI-Generated Digital Products (Verdict: Surprisingly Good)

Ebooks, templates, prompt packs, notion dashboards, mini-courses. AI makes it possible to create these in hours instead of weeks. I used Claude to draft a 40-page ebook on productivity systems for freelancers, designed a cover with Midjourney, and listed it on Gumroad for $17. In the first month it made $340 from 20 sales with zero advertising — just a few posts on Reddit and one Medium article that linked to it. The key is specificity. A generic ebook about productivity will not sell. An ebook called “The 3-Hour Workday System for Freelance Designers” sells because it solves a specific problem for a specific person. Use AI to produce the content fast, but use your own brain to identify the niche. That combination is where the money is.

5\. AI-Assisted Freelance Development (Verdict: The Winner)

This is the one that changed everything for me. I am not a professional developer. I know basic HTML and CSS and can read JavaScript without fully understanding it. But with AI coding assistants — Claude, Cursor, GitHub Copilot — I can now build things that would have taken a senior developer days, and I can do it in hours. I started taking small web projects on Fiverr and Upwork. Landing pages, small business websites, simple booking systems. AI handles the heavy lifting while I focus on understanding the client’s needs, managing communication, and reviewing the output. My effective hourly rate went from essentially zero to over $60 per hour within three months. More importantly, the skills compound. Every project teaches me something new about how to prompt better, how to review AI-generated code, how to spot errors before they reach the client. This is not about replacing developers. It is about a new type of worker — the AI-assisted builder — who can deliver real value without a computer science degree.This is the one that changed things for me. I am not a professional developer, but with AI coding tools — Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude — I can now build things that would have taken a senior developer weeks. Websites, internal dashboards, simple apps, browser extensions. I started offering this on Fiverr and through direct outreach to local businesses. The results were dramatic. AI does not replace the need to understand what the client actually wants or to communicate clearly. But it eliminates most of the implementation time. I went from knowing basic HTML to delivering full React websites with backend integrations in three months. My average project now earns between $500 and $1,500. Last month was my first $4,000 month. The key learning: AI multiplies your existing skills. If you already understand design, writing, marketing, or basic tech, AI can take you from amateur to professional-level output in months, not years.

What I Learned From All of This

The AI side hustles that fail are the ones where AI does all the thinking. Generating generic content, spinning up identical products, copying what everyone else is doing. The market sees through this instantly. The ones that work are where a human brings judgment, taste, or relationship skills — and uses AI to execute ten times faster than before. Nobody is being replaced by AI right now. People are being replaced by other people who use AI better. That gap is your opportunity. Pick one skill you already have. Find one problem in one specific market. Use AI to deliver the solution faster and cheaper than anyone else could manually. That is the entire playbook. Everything else is noise.
